_comment: Config for tools/equipment_evaluator (AIR DOMAIN, REPORT-ONLY).
Every knob the decision algorithm reads lives here. Nothing in this file
is written back to the mod - the evaluator never modifies mod content.

stat_model._comment: See stats.py for the derivation of the stacking formula.

range_targets._comment: Minimum acceptable air_range (km) for a generation transition to clear the range gate. 'default' applies to any role not listed.

_comment: Primary HOI4 air mission each role is scored as flying. This selects
which `mission_type_stats` blocks on a module apply (radar surface
detection, torpedo naval_strike_targetting, interception air_attack,
ordnance agility penalties). One mission per role, not a set: a design
is scored as if doing one job, and applying every overlapping block
would double-count. Both sides of a transition use the same mission,
so the comparison stays fair whichever mission is chosen.
Signed weights over stats. Score of a design vs another is
gain = SUM_s w_s * (new_s - old_s) / max(|old_s|, floor_s)
normalised by SUM |w_s|, so gain is a dimensionless fraction.
Negative weight = lower is better (cost). air_range is deliberately
absent: it is the gate, not a scored stat.

stat_relative_floors._comment: Denominator floor per stat when computing relative change, so a 0 -> small change does not produce an infinite gain.

_comment: min_net_gain: weighted gain (fraction) below which a new generation that
DOES clear the range gate is only a marginal improvement (noted, still SWITCH).
range_override_gain: gain required to adopt a new generation that MISSES the
range target and cannot be redesigned to reach it. Below this -> KEEP_OLD.
Many 1930s airframes physically cannot reach 1000 km; this is what stops the
tool from freezing every early-war line on its first design.
redesign_min_gain: minimum gain of the redesigned variant over the OLD
generation for SWITCH_REDESIGNED to be preferred over KEEP_OLD.
max_redesign_sacrifice: how much weighted combat score the range-restoring
variant may give up relative to the new default design before the redesign
is rejected as 'range at any price' (it is still reported in the CSV).
range_recovery_max_sacrifice: the range gate is otherwise one-sided - it
checks only the NEW design, and air_range is deliberately not a scored
stat, so a step that lifts a design OVER the target reads as a pure
regression (it was marking the mod's own Fix 47 / Fix 49 long-range
variants KEEP_OLD). When the old design was below target and the new one
is at or above it, the step is adopted provided it gives up no more than
this much weighted combat score - the same 'range at any price' guard
max_redesign_sacrifice applies to the redesign search.

resource_significance._comment: Per-unit resource increase (new minus old) at or above which a switch is flagged SWITCH_CONDITIONAL so it can be gated on economy state at runtime.

_comment: Descending multipliers applied to the group's historical maximum design factor.
The geometric 1/3/10 ladder makes the best affordable design dominant even if
the engine treats priority as a weight, while every lower rank remains a live fallback.
Line-efficiency retention factors mirror common/defines/05_defines.lua.
A full switch below full_switch_min_retention is forbidden by default:
keep mature lines and put only newly available factories on the new model.
efficiency_penalty_weight converts the immediate lost-output fraction into
the same dimensionless space as the weighted equipment gain.

infantry._comment: Infantry-equipment scoring. Negative build_cost_ic means cheaper is better.

_comment: Complete integrated scoring for tanks, artillery and vehicles.
Thresholds are hard minimums. Tanks may search legal non-armament module
replacements to recover them; non-modular equipment cannot be redesigned.
Module search that tries to restore range on the new airframe.
candidate_scope: 'country' = modules referenced anywhere in this
country's own *_planes.txt at or before the new generation index,
plus every module whose name has no country prefix (generic).
max_slot_changes: how many slots may be altered at once.
range_module_categories: category name substrings that mark a module as
range-relevant (fuel/drop tanks). Engine swaps are handled separately.

paths._comment: All paths are relative to the mod root (auto-detected as tools/../ unless --mod-root is given).
